sentences.text: Hon'Ble Sri Justice C.V.Bhaskar Reddy

Writ Petition No.706 of 2024
Order:

This Writ Petition, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, is filed by the petitioner seeking the following relief:
"...to issue appropriate writ, or direction particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring (i) the action of the Respondent No.2 in issuing notice dated 27.12.2023 vide No.DUBA/CONS/405/346/2023 in impounding/ revoking the Petitioner's passport bearing No. 26486883 without following the due process of law on the ground of pending chargesheet filed in Crime No. 133 of 2021 on the file of Raidurgam Police Station as illegal, arbitrary, unconstitutional, in violation of Principles of Natural Justice and contrary to the provisions of Passports Act, 1967 and consequently set aside the impugned notice dated 27.12.2023 vide No.DUBA/CONS/405/346/2023 issued by Respondent No.2 (ii) the action of Respondent No.2 in not considering the Petitioner's reply dated 05.01.2024 in response to the impugned notice dated 27.12.2023 as illegal, arbitrary,
unconstitutional and violative of principles of natural justice and consequently direct the Respondents not to interfere with the rights and personal liberties of the Petitioner in taking harsh steps such as impounding/revoking Petitioner's Passport bearing No. Z6486883.
2.
The case of the petitioner is that he travelled to Dubai on 03.11.2020 and working as a Manager and Consultant in Kypto Master Technology in Dubai, United Arab Emirates.

It is further case of the petitioner that he was holding Passport bearing No.L3766049, which expired on 16.07.2023 and on submission of renewal application, the respondent Nos.3 and 4 after verification, issued fresh passport bearing No.Z6486883, which is valid till 02.10.2023.

It is further case of the petitioner that respondent No.2 had issued impugned show-cause notice, dated 27.12.2023 vide No.Duba/Cons/405/346/2023 intimating about the pendency of Crime No.133/2021 registered for the offences under Sections 406 and 420 IPC and called for explanation from the petitioner within 10 days as to why his passport should not be impounded/ revoked under Section 10(3)(b), 10(3)(e)
and 10(3)(h) of the Passports Act, 1967 and to produce a "No objection to issue passport or Acquittal Order" in the criminal/civil/police case from the Court in India as per GSR No.570(E) dated 25.08.1993.

It is also case of the petitioner that on enquiry, he came to know that he was arrayed as Accused No.1 in the said Crime No.133/2021 and after completion of investigation, charge sheet was filed against Accused No.2 on the file of XIII Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Cyberabad at Azaan Ali Syed vs Union Of India on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181428234/
1 Rajendranagar, vide C.C.No.886 of 2022 and the petitioner/ Accused No.1 and Accused No.3 were shown as absconding.

It is also the case of the petitioner that he submitted detailed reply dated 05.01.2024 to the impugned notice through email but so far the respondents have not considered the same.
3.

Heard the submissions of Sri Dammalapati Srinivas, learned Senior Counsel appearing for Sri M.S.Achyuth Bharthwaj, learned counsel for the petitioner, Smt. N. Rajya Lakshmi, learned counsel representing Sri Gadi Praveen Kumar, learned Deputy Solicitor General of India appearing for respondents and perused the record.

4. It is the contention of the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner that mere pendency of the criminal case against the petitioner cannot be a ground to deny issuance of passport to the petitioner.

It is further contention of the learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner that in catena of judgments, the Apex Court as well as this Court held that "passport authority cannot refuse renewal of the passport on the ground of pendency of criminal case and directed the passport authority to issue the passport without raising the objection relating to pendency of the criminal case."

Since after verification, the passport of the petitioner was renewed, the respondent No.2 cannot issue impugned show cause notice dated 27.12.2023 insisting to surrender the passport and the said action on the part of the respondents is contrary to the procedure laid down in the Passports Act,
1967.
5.

In view of the settled law in Vangala Kasturi Rangacharyulu v. Central Bureau of Investigation 1;
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India 2 and Satish Chandra Verma v. Union of India and others 3 mere pendency of the criminal case is not a ground to decline issuance of the passport to the petitioner or direct to surrender of the passport on the alleged ground of suppression of material information.

sentences.text:
It may be noted that the petitioner had submitted reply dated 05.01.2024 to the impugned show cause notice dated 27.12.2023.
6.

Since it is the case of the petitioner that his passport was already renewed by the respondents,
ends of justice would be met if the respondents are directed not to insist the petitioner to surrender his passport bearing No.L366049, subject to the following conditions:-
1.

The petitioner shall submit an undertaking before the respondent No.2-Consulate General of India, Dubai, stating that he will appear before the learned XIII Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Cyberabad at Rajendranagar, in C.C.No.886 of 2022.

entities.text: XIII Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Cyberabad at Rajendranagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: On filing such undertaking, the respondent No.2 shall not insist the petitioner to surrender his passport and permit the petitioner to travel to India.

On arrival to India, the petitioner shall submit an undertaking along with an affidavit in C.C.No.886 of 2022 in XIII Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Cyberabad at Rajendranagar,
stating that he will not leave India during pendency of the said C.C. without permission of the Court and that he will cooperate with the trial Court in concluding the proceedings in the said C.C.

sentences.text: However, liberty is granted to the petitioner to file an application before the trial Court seeking permission to travel abroad and it is for the trial Court to consider the same in accordance with law.
7. Accordingly, this Writ Petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
